requirements.text: The CAMRAD-AEB shall not have its effectiveness adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 06 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The CAMRAD-AEB as an electronic control system shall meet the safety aspects requirements of Annex 3 of UN R152.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide a failure warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.4 when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of the Regulation from being met.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall not have an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check and shall not delay illuminating the warning signal in the case of an electrically detectable failure.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall illuminate the failure warning signal defined in paragraph 5.1.4.1 upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition such as sensor blindness or sensor misalignment.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall indicate to the driver the non-initialised status if the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, and this information shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall give a deactivation warning as specified in paragraph 5.4.3 when the system is deactivated, where the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide the emergency braking interventions described in paragraphs 5.2.1.2 and 5.2.2.2 having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle, subject to paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals and to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision, demonstrated in the assessment under Annex 3 including the scenarios of Appendix 2.

The vehicle fitted with the CAMRAD-AEB shall meet the performance requirements of UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments and shall be equipped with an anti-lock braking function in accordance with Annex 6 to UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1, triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking, when an imminent collision with a preceding M1 vehicle in the same lane is detected with a relative speed above that up to which the subject vehicle is able to avoid the collision.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1 no later than the start of emergency braking intervention where the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of the emergency braking.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall issue a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a vehicle.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall, in the absence of driver input that would lead to interruption under paragraph 5.3.2 and under the conditions (a) to (d) of paragraph 5.2.1.4, achieve a relative impact speed no greater than the maximum relative impact speed for M1 vehicles in the table of paragraph 5.2.1.4.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall meet a maximum relative impact speed of 0 km/h up to a relative speed of 40 km/h, 10 km/h at 42 km/h, 15 km/h at 45 km/h, 25 km/h at 50 km/h, 30 km/h at 55 km/h and 35 km/h at 60 km/h for both maximum mass and mass in running order conditions, applying the value assigned to the next higher relative speed for intermediate relative speeds.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1 no later than the start of emergency braking intervention when the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed of 5 km/h within the conditions of paragraph 5.2.2.4.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall issue a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a pedestrian.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall, under the conditions (a) to (e) of paragraph 5.2.2.4, achieve an impact speed no greater than 0 km/h for subject vehicle speeds of 20 to 40 km/h, 10 km/h at 42 km/h (maximum mass only), 15 km/h at 45 km/h, 25 km/h at 50 km/h, 30 km/h at 55 km/h and 35 km/h at 60 km/h, applying the next higher speed value for intermediate speeds.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide the means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning and the emergency braking.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall allow the interruption to be initiated by any positive action, such as kick-down or operating the direction indicator control, that indicates the driver is aware of the emergency situation.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain where a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function is provided.
The CAMRAD-AEB control shall be designed such that manual deactivation is not possible with less than two deliberate actions.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall not be manually deactivatable at a speed above 10 km/h.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to its automatic deactivation are no longer present.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall inform the driver by a constant optical warning signal, which may be the yellow warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4, that the AEBS function has been deactivated.
The collision warning of paragraphs 5.2.1.1 and 5.2.2.1 shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.
The CAMRAD-AEB failure warning referred to in paragraph 5.1.4.1 shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.

Each CAMRAD-AEB optical warning signal shall be activated when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or to the manufacturer-designated check position, except for signals shown in a common space.
The CAMRAD-AEB optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight and their satisfactory condition shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall provide a constant optical warning signal, which may be the failure warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4, when indicating to the driver that the AEBS is temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall allow confirmation of its correct operational status at a Periodic Technical Inspection by visible observation of the failure warning signal status following a power-ON and any bulb check.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall detect and respond to the M1 category vehicle target defined in paragraph 6.3.1 used for the vehicle detection tests, or an equivalent soft target according to ISO 19206-3:2021.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall detect and respond to the child articulated soft pedestrian target according to ISO 19206-2:2018 used for the pedestrian detection tests.

The CAMRAD-AEB failure warning signal shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h with a simulated electrical failure, and shall be reactivated immediately after a subsequent ignition "off"/"on" cycle with the vehicle stationary as long as the failure exists.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall meet the required performance in two test runs of each test scenario, with the number of failed test runs not exceeding 10.0 per cent of the performed Car to Car tests and 10.0 per cent of the performed Car to Pedestrian tests.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be covered by an approval mark affixed to the vehicle marked with C for Car to Car and P for Car to Pedestrian pursuant to UN Regulation No. 152.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall be documented by a documentation package giving access to its basic design, the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems, its functions and safety concept, and how its current operational status can be checked for periodic technical inspections.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall warn the driver by a warning signal or message display in case of a failure, and the warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists when the system is not deactivated by the driver.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall inhibit all output control signals associated with the higher level function when the chosen provision under fault conditions removes that function, in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall incorporate measures ensuring it does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions such as climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress or ice packing, and these measures shall be documented.

The braking equipment used by the CAMRAD-AEB shall not have its effectiveness adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements of Regulation No. 10.
The CAMRAD-AEB, as a system using the braking system for automatically commanded braking, shall meet the safety aspects requirements of Annex 8 of UN R13-H.
The CAMRAD-AEB shall be designed so that malfunctions of the electric control transmission do not apply the brakes contrary to the intentions of the driver.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall generate the stop lamp signal when its automatically commanded braking produces a deceleration greater than 1.3 m/s², and may generate it at or below that value; once generated the signal shall be kept as long as the deceleration demand persists and may be suppressed at standstill or when the demand falls below 1.3 m/s².

The CAMRAD-AEB shall not activate the emergency braking signal below 6 m/s² deceleration, may generate it at or above this value as defined by the manufacturer, and shall de-activate it at the latest when the deceleration has fallen below 2.5 m/s².

The vehicle fitted with the CAMRAD-AEB shall have broadband radiated emissions below 32 dBµV/m in 30 to 75 MHz, 32 to 43 dBµV/m in 75 to 400 MHz and 43 dBµV/m in 400 to 1,000 MHz when measured per Annex 4 at a 10.0 ± 0.2 m antenna spacing.

The vehicle fitted with the CAMRAD-AEB shall have narrowband radiated emissions below 28 dBµV/m in 30 to 230 MHz and 35 dBµV/m in 230 to 1,000 MHz when measured per Annex 5 at a 10.0 ± 0.2 m antenna spacing.

The CAMRAD-AEB shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions when the vehicle is exposed to field strengths of 30 V/m over 90 per cent and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz band, and 10 V/m over 90 per cent and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.

The CAMRAD-AEB ESA shall withstand, over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band, 60 V/m stripline (20 to 400 MHz), 75 V/m TEM cell (20 to 200 MHz), 60 mA BCI (20 to 400 MHz), 30 V/m ALSE (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 21 V/m reverberation chamber (LUF to 2,000 MHz) below 2 GHz, and 10 V/m ALSE and 7 V/m reverberation chamber in 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.

The CAMRAD-AEB ESA shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band, minimum levels of 50 V/m stripline, 62.5 V/m TEM cell, 50 mA BCI, 25 V/m ALSE and 18 V/m reverberation chamber below 2 GHz, and 8 V/m ALSE and 6 V/m reverberation chamber in 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.

The CAMRAD-AEB ESA on the 12 V supply lines shall not emit transient conducted disturbances exceeding a maximum positive pulse amplitude of +75 V and a maximum negative pulse amplitude of -100 V, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10.

The CAMRAD-AEB ESA shall meet, for its immunity related functions on the 12 V system, test pulse 1 at -75 V (500 pulses, FPSC III), 2a at +37 V (500 pulses, FPSC I), 2b at +10 V (10 pulses, FPSC II), 3a at -112 V (1 h, FPSC I) and 3b at +75 V (1 h, FPSC I) according to ISO 7637-2.
